messages:
Lina (Customer): Hey support — our integration started returning 500s around 14:02 UTC. We don't see a request_id in the response body. What exact bits should we send you to speed debugging?

Sam (Support): sorry about that — we can take a look. The minimum we need: a single request/trace reference (x-request-id or similar), a short curl that reproduces the call, and a brief timeline (first/last timestamps you observed). If you can attach a HAR or SDK logs that helps too.

Lina (Customer): where do I find x-request-id when using the Node SDK? The response object doesn't show it by default.

Sam (Support): in Node, you can grab headers from the raw response. Example (pseudo):

```js
const res = await client.generate(payload)
// if using low-level fetch wrapper
console.log(res.headers.get('x-request-id'))
// or your SDK may expose res.requestId or res.metadata.request_id
```

If you see a header called x-request-id or request-id that's the trace token we use. If it's absent, include a full SDK debug log (see below).

Lina (Customer): browser client — how to capture?

Sam (Support): open DevTools > Network, click the failing request, copy the response headers. Better: right-click > Save all as HAR with content. Attach the HAR file; redact Authorization header. In HAR we can find the request/response pair and the response header x-request-id.

Lina (Customer): mobile Android app — we only have app logs and a proxy (Charles). Anything special?

Marco (SRE): for mobile we look for whichever token your proxy logs show (often header). If using the mobile SDK, enable verbose logging for a short window and capture a log snippet around the error. Example log lines we look for:

"INFO request sent route=/v1/generate request_id=abc123 duration_ms=502 status=500"

If you only have Charles/Proxied capture, export a HAR from it.

Lina (Customer): can you share a minimal CURL I can paste into our CI to reproduce?

Sam (Support): yup — replace AUTH and PAYLOAD, then run. Remember to remove any sensitive data before sending.

```bash
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-small","input":"hello"}'
```

When you run with `-v` we want the response headers block which includes x-request-id if the server set it. If you get a 500 without that header, capture the full `-v` output and the timestamp.

Lina (Customer): any preferred redaction pattern?

Sam (Support): yes — replace the bearer token with `<REDACTED_TOKEN>` and any customer PII in the payload with `[...]`. Keep the request_id/trace token intact (that's what we need).

Lina (Customer): what if we can't reproduce reliably — intermittent 500s?

Marco (SRE): capture one or two failing samples with timestamps and the request/trace tokens. Also share a short sample of your retry/backoff config. If you can toggle SDK debug logging for 5 minutes during a spike, send that bundle. We have tooling to correlate logs by timestamp if the token is missing.

Lina (Customer): how do I produce the SDK debug bundle?

Sam (Support): steps:
1) enable verbose logging in your SDK (env var or client option) for ~5m
2) reproduce the error or wait for it
3) grab the logs + a HAR or curl + local application logs around the time
4) attach them to this thread or upload to the secure upload link we'll provide

If you prefer UI: open Redwood Console > Observability > Requests and search around the timestamp. That view will show request traces and any associated request id — copy that id and paste it here.

Lina (Customer): ok attaching a short `curl -v` output and a tiny HAR in a sec. One more: do you need model id and region?

Sam (Support): yes please include model identifier, region (e.g., us-east-1), and the full timestamp (UTC). Also any tenant/api-key id (not the key itself) helps us find entries in our logs faster.

DebugBot: automated note — if you include a request id we can try to auto-correlate logs; use the single request id per file to speed processing.

Marco (SRE): thanks @Lina — once you drop the artifacts here we'll triage and follow up with a short repro checklist or ask for a short live session if needed. :thumbsup:
